newsitem.title: ITALY: Banca di Roma sees swift deal on layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Banca di Roma sees swift deal on layoffs.

text.p: Banca di Roma chairman Cesare Geronzi said on Monday he was optimistic that a deal could be reached soon on layoffs.
The Banca di Roma group, which includes Banca Nazionale dell'Agricoltura and Banca Mediterranea, is planning more than 4,000 layoffs in a group restructuring programme.
Several hundred staff staged a strike earlier this month in protest at the plans.
"We are confident we'll wrap up the talks soon," Geronzi told reporters on the sidelines of a conference in Rome.
Leaders of Italy's banking association ABI held talks with the government and unions earlier this month to try to resolve a deadlock over planned layoffs throughout the banking sector.
Analysts say the Italian banking sector is hugely overstaffed and radical restructuring is needed if it is to achieve the sort of profitability seen elsewhere in Europe.
Geronzi told the conference in a speech earlier that "companies cannot survive in a world market without having recourse to flexibility" -- that is, deregulation and greater competitivity.
